candidates.label: Ptolemais (Phoenician coast)
candidates.support: A Phoenician coastal city, identified with the Old Testament's Acco. Pleiades, OpenBible.info and Wikidata agree on the site, known today as Acre (Akko).

summary.text: Ptolemais was the most prominent city on the Phoenician coast in the time of the Maccabees, built on the site of the Old Testament's Acco. Acts records that Paul's ship, nearing the end of its voyage from Tyre, finished its course at Ptolemais, where Paul and his companions greeted the brothers and stayed with them one day before traveling on to Caesarea.

history.text: The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia identifies Ptolemais as the same city as Acco, named in the book of Judges, and notes that the city is mentioned several times in the books of the Maccabees as a leading town of the Phoenician coast.

otConnections.note: Judges records that the tribe of Asher "didn't drive out the inhabitants of Acco," the Canaanite town on this site that was later refounded under the Greek name Ptolemais.

politicalHistory.entity: Roman province of Syria (ruler: Imperial legates, governed from Antioch)
politicalHistory.note: Administers the Cilician plain throughout, and administered Philip's former tetrarchy directly for a few years after his death (34-37; Antiquities 18.4.6).
